classification: DECISION VERIFICATION AND UNIQUENESS AUDIT; NO CANDIDATE, NO SUBMISSION, NO EXPERIMENT
hypothesis: Why did GEMSDOE32 (USER-REPORTED 0.2778) score above its D2.8 family, and can any file pass the uniqueness rule while scoring above it? Not a geological hypothesis test.
mechanism: The 0.2778 file equals the D2.8 reference with its 6,436 catalogue-adjacent dots removed (all within 3 px of a labelled catalogue fault). Under the expected-count model with alpha+beta=1, removing dots raises DTI iff their mean hit probability is below alpha times DTI (DERIVED; a bound of 0.052 from the user-reported 0.2600). The hidden test set is new faults not in the USGS database (OFFICIAL-PAGE-TEXT).
named_non_fault_mimic: Mapping-coverage gap: areas with no USGS fault mapping because survey coverage is sparse. Not tested; no candidate exists.
hypothesis_status: Explanation of a user-reported score only. No candidate was generated and no new method was tested. Ranked hypotheses are in research/2026-10-31-decision-verification-and-hypotheses.md section 6.

GEMSDOE32 fails the rho clause as well: Spearman 0.9236 against D2.8 (above 0.90).
The uploaded file behind the portal error 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]' is unknown; the repo's files are in range and cannot reproduce it.
No organizer-authenticated template or data is available; the hidden test cannot be measured locally.
